claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on hypothesis statements only: Johnson's three hypotheses (VASO-E013, context) and the essay's relay of the clinging-as-latch identification (VASO-E038, context). The critical report's qualifier (VASO-E017) shows the latch literature addresses none of the three criteria biological memory requires — input-dependent state, later readout, discrimination among prior inputs — and that the only demonstrated write–store–read loop in a living flow network is in a slime mold. No admitted record bears on the attribution in either direction.

treatment.plainLanguage: The grip in your blood vessels is part of how your mind holds an expectation — and what Buddhists call clinging is that grip.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If shown, this would be a new biological memory mechanism and would decide the case's grand attribution; but nothing in the ledger tests it, so at present it decides nothing.
treatment.strongestObjection: A thermostat has hysteresis without an autobiography; vascular smooth muscle retaining tone contains information about its history in the trivial dynamical sense, and no experiment shows a vessel storing a prediction, reading it back, or discriminating between prior inputs.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An animal preparation in which different induced vascular states, with oxygenation clamped, produce reliably different later neural responses to identical stimulation after the initiating input has stopped (VASO-R005).
A clean negative in that design — neural gain tracking only instantaneous perfusion — which would collapse the claim to ordinary neurovascular physiology.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The attribution is stated by its proponents (VASO-E013, VASO-E037, context) and audited at grade D by the critical report: no study identifies a smooth-muscle latch at any tender point and no time-resolved release has been imaged (VASO-E016, undermines). The case's own study lands against the named compartment: no arteriole's energetic cost has ever been measured (VASO-E019) and pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation, not a dephosphorylated hold (VASO-E020). The Doppler footprint proponents read as a clenched upstream vessel is, by its authors' account, as compatible with contracture compressing the bed (VASO-E027, weighed at zero diagnosticity). The second essay's relocation of the vascular element (VASO-E044, VASO-E045) rests on an unread source and carries no weight. Unresolved rather than contradicted because none of the arteriole studies withdrew its stimulus, so input-free persistence was untestable in them.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a tiny artery inside the muscle held clenched by a low-energy lock, starving its neighborhood — not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis; every account competes with it directly, and the tests that would decide it (latch at a tender point, cold knot on PET, blood before stiffness, breath-gated release) are specified and unrun.
treatment.strongestObjection: The mechanism is borrowed from conduit arteries and, where the hypothesis needs it, the published measurements show sustained activation rather than an economical latch; the vascular abnormalities at real trigger points are partial, conduit-scale, and explicable by mechanical compression.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
A palpated knot stiff on elastography, active on EMG and metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Time-resolved imaging showing perfusion rising before stiffness falls at a felt release (VASO-R001) — or its absence.
The non-latching motor-protein phenotype found throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, which would retire the intramuscular form.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not read and verified; no admitted evidence record bears on the claim. It is featured as a serious competing mechanism — a knot held by vessel tone, a hyaluronan collar and a fascial tether, needing no latch — not because anything supports it.

treatment.plainLanguage: What holds a knot is not one lock but three stacked together: the vessel's tone, a collar of gelled lubricant around it, and the tether that pins the skin's fascia to the tissue beneath.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If the three-element hold were shown, it would relocate the vascular account to the skin and absorb pressure-alone release; nothing yet tests it, and its cheapest test is an afternoon with a pencil Doppler.
treatment.strongestObjection: The graded stiff regions blinded sonographers measure lie inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin, and the account's only source is a proponent's AI-generated essay the ledger has not been able to read.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with Doppler-mapped perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
A knot released by saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath and no pressure (VASO-R017).
Release events showing three separable time constants in perfusion, stiffness and interfascial glide — or their absence.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The sole record is the founding essay's own uncited assertion that traditional maps place the important knots along the torso's midline and limbs (VASO-E039, weak, supports); it supplies no coding rule and no chance baseline. No blinded anatomical coding has been done, and even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches.

treatment.plainLanguage: The knots and channels of Tibetan, Indian and Chinese body-maps are accurate first-hand descriptions of the same tension system, felt from the inside by trained practitioners.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An alignment of traditional knot locations with vascular or fascial geography would be suggestive but would not discriminate between latch, perforator and guarding accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is the weakest kind of evidence; until the traditional locations are coded blind and tested against chance, every convergence is vulnerable to post-hoc matching.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered blinded coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with perforators, sympathetic chains or fascial anchor lines above chance (VASO-R006).
The same coding finding no alignment beyond chance, which would retire the convergence argument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The latch-bridge model is textbook smooth-muscle physiology (VASO-E003, strong): high sustained stress at low phosphorylation in conduit-artery preparations. The case's study qualifies its generality — latch behaviour was present in the rabbit femoral artery and absent in its own saphenous branch, and the comparison was never followed downstream (VASO-E021). The essay's restatement (VASO-E034) overstates the model as zero rather than low activation.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle can lock its grip and hold tension cheaply after the signal that started it fades.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Established physiology that all accounts accept; it decides nothing between them until it is shown in the vessels a knot would need.
treatment.strongestObjection: Established in large tonic arteries over minutes to hours; not generic across vascular smooth muscle, and unobserved in arterioles.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study showing the latch phenotype persists into skeletal-muscle arterioles — or disappears with caliber (VASO-R004).
Direct energetic measurement of maintained constriction in any arteriole.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The inference — a change completing in seconds is a change of maintained state, not remodeled structure — is stated by the essay (VASO-E035, weak) and rests on physiological priors about remodeling timescales, disclosed here as priors. Its premise, an objective seconds-scale local event, is unmeasured; the nearest imaged change is shrinkage and falling pulsatility over visits after needling in three cases (VASO-E030, context). 'State' includes guarding and densification, not only vessels.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really lets go in seconds, it was something the body was doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Separates state from scar for all three accounts but does not separate a vascular state from a neuromuscular or fascial one.
treatment.strongestObjection: The premise is the unmeasured thing: no time-resolved record shows any objective local event within seconds of a felt release.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography and Doppler at a felt release showing a step change within seconds (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, which would remove the premise.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay, p. 3); no admitted evidence record bears on it, and the primary densification literature has not been retrieved. Its timescale — the question that matters — is unknown to the ledger.

treatment.plainLanguage: The sticky, thickened lubricant between fascial layers can be thinned again by pressure, movement and warmth.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within a session under pressure alone, the knot can be a state without being a vessel, and pressure-only release is exactly what to expect; if it reverses over hours, the vascular accounts remain the only fast candidates.
treatment.strongestObjection: No retrieved study reports reversal on a seconds-to-minutes timescale, and the causal link between densification and a painful trigger point is unproven.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieved primary data on hyaluronan viscosity change under load and warmth with a measured timescale (VASO-R008).
Stiffness dropping at a release with no perfusion change — the densification signature — in the keystone rig.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Proposed as a hypothesis in 2008 (VASO-E004, context) and given a demonstrated mechanism in 2024: physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neurons through mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005, strong). Instantaneous modulation in brain, not storage, and not the human periphery.

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood vessels don't just feed neurons; their mechanical state can change what nearby neurons do.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Establishes a read path exists somewhere; it does not show vessels store anything or that the effect operates at a tender point.
treatment.strongestObjection: A mechanism of instantaneous nudging in rat brain says nothing about history-dependent readout or about peripheral tissue.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Demonstration of history-dependent vascular influence on neural responses with metabolic variables clamped (VASO-R005).
Peripheral mechanosensory endings shown to read arteriolar caliber changes at a tender point.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review documents reproducible rises in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia with slow breathing in healthy humans (VASO-E009, strong); the essay restates it uncited (VASO-E036). Global cardiovascular indices only; no local tissue measurement.

treatment.plainLanguage: Slow breathing with a long exhale reliably tilts the nervous system toward its calming branch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A global shift every account accepts; the local, site-specific unlatching the hypothesis adds has never been measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: Measured on the heart in people with no tender point in the study; it says nothing about a vessel at a knot.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local perfusion or stiffness change time-locked to the exhale at a palpated site and not a sham (VASO-R001, VASO-R016).
Equal clearance under held breath and slow exhalation (VASO-R020), which would leave the global shift a felt correlate.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review finds manual examination not shown reliable or valid with no accepted reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the leading critique argues the construct is circular (VASO-E010); proponent groups concede it — examination results vary with training (VASO-E029), there is no gold standard and palpation variability cannot be trained away (VASO-E078, VASO-E079), and imaging confirmed 71.5% of one examiner's palpated spots (VASO-E081; VASO-E080 context).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners can't reliably agree on where a trigger point is, there is no gold standard for what one is, and experts dispute whether the concept holds up.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Weakens the observation base of every account equally; it is why any decisive experiment must fix sites blind and by instrument.
treatment.strongestObjection: Reliability of the manual exam is not the reliability of instrumented detection; blinded sonographers do find graded stiffness at palpated sites.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A validated instrumented reference standard with demonstrated inter-examiner reliability.
A census with pain-free controls showing imaging picks out palpated spots above chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Common experience and proponent report (VASO-E015, weak), a second-hand 1986 prevalence estimate for a pain syndrome (VASO-E028, weak), and one population record: two people reporting no pain had eleven or more tender points in a pain-selected community sample (VASO-E082, weak; VASO-E083 context). The critical report shows the existence and reproducibility of the discrete spot are themselves disputed (VASO-E012). The whole-body scanner (VASO-E018) bears on feasibility of a census, not on the claim.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, very tender spots in muscle and fascia are common in ordinary people.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: All accounts predict tender spots; their existence decides nothing about mechanism.
treatment.strongestObjection: No census has ever been taken, the one survey is pain-selected and tests fixed sites, and the reliability of finding a 'spot' is unproven.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An unselected community tender-point survey with count distributions (VASO-R010).
A knot census with pain-free controls, children and long-term meditators (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Sustained spontaneous activity in a 1–2 mm nidus of every trigger point and none in adjacent non-tender fibers (VASO-E001, moderate). Simons 2002 qualifies exclusivity: endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites and never off the zone (VASO-E031), so the claim as worded — more prevalent at trigger points within the zone, absent outside it — is what survives. The essay's restatement (VASO-E043) and the equine cross-species note (VASO-E052, unread source) add no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points hum with ongoing electrical activity more often than nearby quiet spots in the same nerve-supply zone — and never where there is no such zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the knot is actively maintained, but the signature lives in the skeletal endplate zone first, which is what the guarding account predicts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Endplate noise is a property of the endplate zone; the trigger point may simply be where an examiner presses within it.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Needle EMG with a matched endplate-zone control under mental arithmetic (VASO-R011).
Retrieval of the phentolamine and relaxation primaries showing autonomic modulation of the nidus (VASO-R009, VASO-R012).

claimAssessments.reasoning: One record: mental arithmetic raised trigger-point EMG while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet in fourteen subjects (VASO-E002, moderate); the essay's restatement (VASO-E033) adds nothing. Same lineage as VASO-E001, never replicated, no vascular measurement, and the control needle was not placed in a matched endplate-zone site — an inference drawn from VASO-E031 on the sibling claim VASO-C002, disclosed as such.

treatment.plainLanguage: Doing arithmetic in your head turns up the electrical activity inside one tender point and not a centimeter away.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The 'write' half of any storage account, and the strongest evidence of central addressing; but sympathetic drive to endplates fits it without any vessel.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control may have lain off the endplate zone, so the stressor may have selected any endplate-zone site rather than the tender one.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The trigger point rising and a matched endplate-zone control staying quiet under arithmetic — or both rising (VASO-R011).
A skin-perfusion fall over the point and not over control skin during the stressor (VASO-R016).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in a source (SRC-JHONG-2026A) the ledger has not read; no admitted evidence record bears on it. Featured as the perforator account's reading of the stress result.

treatment.plainLanguage: When stress lights up a trigger point, what the brain is doing is clamping the skin's blood vessels in one small territory — the way a person blushes in one place.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would distinguish the perforator account from both the intramuscular latch and skeletal guarding as the explanation of the stressor result.
treatment.strongestObjection: The stressor result was recorded by a needle in muscle; nothing measured skin perfusion, and the reading exists only in an unread proponent essay.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A localized fall in skin perfusion over the tender point and not over control skin during mental arithmetic (VASO-R016).
Global or absent perfusion change under the stressor.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One record: first-person and practitioner testimony from the hypothesis's proponent, in an AI-generated essay (VASO-E014, weak). Real evidence that people feel a release; no evidence of any tissue event. Expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person report.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press on a knot, breathe out slowly, and within seconds it feels as if it lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The anchor phenomenon of the case; until an objective local correlate is measured, it cannot discriminate between any accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: A felt release is exactly what expectation riding on a global parasympathetic shift would produce, with nothing local happening at all.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved imaging of a felt release with a local stiffness drop and perfusion rise exceeding sham and pressure-only controls (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor — the essay's practitioner report (p. 3) — with no admitted supporting record. Its one admitted evidence record, VASO-E067 (direction context, moderate), establishes that a published pressure-only compression protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation anywhere in its methods or results — and establishes nothing else: its statement carries no outcome, and the outcome and 24-hour non-recurrence figures proposed as records on this claim were refused at review. On VASO-E067 alone the claim is neither supported nor contradicted. The outcomes of that protocol are admitted elsewhere in the ledger, on VASO-C005 (VASO-E072: 60% of active and 86% of latent points undetectable after the first round); VASO-C005 is neither parent nor sibling of this claim, so the disclosed-basis rule does not let that record carry a grade here. The case names it as a lead against the two-key necessity and leaves the grade to VASO-R020, which would supply the missing atomic observation with breath controlled.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pushing on a knot without the slow exhale won't release it — you need both keys.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If pressure alone suffices, the breath is not a necessary key and the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state falls; if held breath blocks release, breath-gating is real and both vascular accounts gain.
treatment.strongestObjection: A published protocol released imaged trigger points by compression with nobody told how to breathe — but its subjects may have exhaled on their own, and its outcomes are not yet admitted as an observation on this claim.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The runners' protocol repeated with breath randomised — free, slow exhale, inhale-and-hold — and clearance rates compared (VASO-R020): equal clearance under held breath would contradict the claim; blocked clearance would support it.
Admission of atomic pressure-only outcome records on this claim from the existing study.
A knot released by hydrodissection with no breath (VASO-R017).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay, p. 31); no admitted evidence record bears on it. No time-resolved Doppler and elastography have been acquired at any release.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases, blood returns first and the tissue softens second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction the vascular accounts make and their rivals do not; observed, it would be the smoking gun; reversed or simultaneous, it would undercut both vascular accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nobody has filmed the seconds; densification or guarding predicts stiffness falling with no perfusion change, and no record yet distinguishes the orderings.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Co-registered elastography and Doppler across many felt releases showing perfusion consistently leading stiffness (VASO-R001).
A laser-speckle perfusion flash preceding stiffness change at a superficial knot (VASO-R016).
Stiffness leading, or no perfusion change at all.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Biochemistry: acidic, mediator-rich milieu at active points, but elevated remotely too, in about nine volunteers (VASO-E006). Stiffness: blinded graded stiff area in the trapezius (VASO-E023) and active/latent differences in the calf by a second method (VASO-E069, VASO-E070, VASO-E071, VASO-E072 — context and qualifier, since there is no control tissue). Flow: higher pulsatility near active points (VASO-E022) but a null resistivity index, indices that cannot classify sites (VASO-E025) and no pain-free controls (VASO-E026). A systematic review characterized second-hand (VASO-E007) and essay restatements (VASO-E042; VASO-E050, VASO-E051 from an unread source) add little.

treatment.plainLanguage: Active trigger points are chemically, mechanically and hemodynamically different from surrounding tissue in measurable ways.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Something objective is there, but every account predicts a stiff, acidic, compressed region; only the order and timescale of change would discriminate.
treatment.strongestObjection: The chemistry is not purely local, the flow signature is partial and conduit-scale, and every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle located by palpation.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrumented site selection (VASO-R002).
FDG-PET showing knots metabolically cold — or hot (VASO-R013).

claimAssessments.reasoning: One strong preregistered record: attention toward a histamine skin prick produced ~1.5-fold smaller, faster-resolving responses in ~90% of 57 volunteers with no arousal difference and higher HRV (VASO-E008). Single lab, very recent; the route is vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes in a tissue the parasympathetic system does not innervate directly (VASO-E041, qualifies). Provisionally rather than well supported pending replication.

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an inflamed spot on your skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter — without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it says nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: Tens of minutes, an immune route, healthy skin, one laboratory — none of the featured mechanisms is touched.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication or failure to replicate.
Demonstration of the same site-specific channel acting on tissue stiffness or perfusion at a tender point within seconds.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Median pulsatility index 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites, sonographers blinded (VASO-E022, moderate). No pain-free control group; 'normal' sites sit in symptomatic muscle (VASO-E026, qualifies). The vessels are pulsatile arteries typically over a millimeter, 1–2 cm from the point.

treatment.plainLanguage: The arteries near active trigger points show flow that surges and falls more sharply with each heartbeat than arteries near normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Compatible with distal constriction, contracture compressing the bed, inflammation or probe pressure; it cannot pick a mechanism.
treatment.strongestObjection: The index cannot classify individual sites, and a second resistance index shows no difference.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Doppler in pain-free controls establishing the normal baseline.
The same waveform vanishing, or not, with a release imaged in time.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 49 palpably normal sites (31%), against 55% of active and 40% of latent (VASO-E022). Those normal sites lie in symptomatic muscle at least 5 cm from a trigger point; whether 31% is a true baseline or spillover cannot be said (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Backward flow between heartbeats shows up near nearly a third of spots that feel perfectly normal — in muscles that have a trigger point somewhere else.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Turns the Doppler signature into a gradient across symptomatic muscle rather than a marker of a knot, which weakens the 'footprint of a clenched vessel' reading.
treatment.strongestObjection: Without pain-free controls the 31% may be spillover from neighbouring points rather than the population baseline.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrograde flow rates measured in pain-free subjects.
A census relating retrograde flow to palpated points across the body.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Blinded vibration sonoelastography: stiff area 0.57, 0.36 and 0.17 cm² at active, latent and normal sites, AUC 0.9 (VASO-E023, moderate). The calf strain-elastography findings are a parallel in another muscle and method, not a replication (VASO-E073, VASO-E074, VASO-E076, VASO-E077, context). Sites were selected by palpation; a single vibration frequency; same NIH lineage as the biochemistry.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stiff region at a trigger point is biggest where it hurts on its own, smaller where it hurts only when pressed, and smallest at normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Objective and graded, but every account predicts stiffness; it does not say what the stiff tissue is.
treatment.strongestObjection: The measured contrast presupposes the palpated classification and comes from one lineage with one method.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with shear-wave elastography and blinded, instrument-fixed sites.
Stiffness tracking perfusion, or not, at an imaged release.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites outside any trigger point (VASO-E032, moderate); abstract only, nonrandomized, unblinded, ten subjects, proponent authors.

treatment.plainLanguage: The electrical hum found at trigger points also shows up at some non-tender spots — if they lie in the muscle's nerve-supply zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Places the signature in the endplate zone first and the trigger point second, which the guarding account predicts and the addressable-nidus reading must answer.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract-only; the four-of-eleven figure has not been replicated.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded repeat with matched endplate-zone controls (VASO-R011).
Amplitude data showing the trigger-point signal differs in kind, not just prevalence.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Endplate noise at none of the taut-band sites outside the endplate zone (VASO-E032, moderate; P = 0.000034 per the abstract); same small unblinded study.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where there is no nerve-supply zone, a tight band of muscle has no electrical hum at all.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Ties the electrical signature to skeletal endplates rather than to tautness or tenderness as such — the conventional reading of the nidus.
treatment.strongestObjection: Abstract-only and unblinded; the endplate zone was located by the same authors who classified the sites.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication with blinded site classification.
Spontaneous activity found at a taut-band site demonstrably off the endplate zone.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No difference in resistivity index between active, latent and normal sites (VASO-E024, moderate), a negative recorded in its own right; within-patient comparison in symptomatic subjects, which the authors say may explain the similarity.

treatment.plainLanguage: One standard Doppler measure of downstream resistance is exactly the same near trigger points as near normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the vascular signature at trigger points is partial, not categorical, which any vascular account must accommodate.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites 5 cm from a trigger point in symptomatic muscle may share its vascular state, masking a real difference.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Resistivity index compared against pain-free controls.
A difference emerging at microvascular rather than conduit-artery caliber.
